text: The Bachelor of Software Engineering Honours (BSEHons) at The Open University of Sri Lanka (OUSL) was first introduced in 2009 by the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Faculty of Engineering Technology. It is the first software engineering degree programme offered in Sri Lanka and the first UGC-approved, industry-oriented software engineering programme offered by a local university. The 2025/2026 academic year is the 17th intake. Since 2021 the Centre for IT Education Services (CITES) coordinates and delivers the programme under the guidance of the Department. The curriculum follows IEEE Computer Society / ACM guidelines and was most recently updated in 2025. The next major curriculum revision takes effect from academic year 2030/2031.

BSEHons is a 4-year specialised degree. The minimum period to complete is four academic years (students with course exemptions are exempt from the minimum period). The maximum period is twelve consecutive academic years from the date of first registration. The programme is delivered in 2 semesters per year with a Final examination at the end of each semester; some courses span both semesters and have their Final examination at the end of the second semester.

BSEHons is NOT a fully online programme. Most lab tests are done on-site. Continuous Assessment Tests (CATs) and Final examinations are held on-site at all regional centres and selected study centres, and on-site CATs and Final examinations are held on weekdays. Interactive Learning Sessions and lab practice sessions are conducted online, mostly via Microsoft Teams or Zoom. OUSL does not conduct regular lectures; students are expected to self-learn using study guides and the Moodle LMS online classroom for each course.

A student who does not have a laptop/PC must come to their registered OUSL centre to do lab work and lab tests. Centres are open Tuesday to Saturday, 9 am to 4 pm. Students are strongly recommended to have regular computer access because many courses involve programming and a computer is needed during training and internship.

Minimum entry qualifications for BSEHons (any one of the following): (1) Three passes in the GCE Advanced Level examination in any three subjects, in any number of sittings, excluding General English and General Information Technology; OR (2) 'C' passes in any three subjects in the Cambridge/Edexcel Advanced Level examination; OR (3) Passes in any three OUSL foundation subjects, or any of the OUSL Advanced Certificates (Science, Apparel Technology, Entrepreneurship, Small Business Management); OR (4) Any other qualification acceptable to the Senate. Any other qualification claimed in lieu of A/L must be equivalent to GCE (A/L) and acceptable to the University and must be submitted with supporting documents before the exemption deadline of 7 December 2025.

Applications for the 2025/2026 intake are open from 15 October 2025 to 30 November 2025. The application fee is Rs. 750.00. Applications are submitted online at https://reginfo.ou.ac.lk/applyonline/; payment can be made online by debit/credit card or at any OUSL Regional or Study Centre. Computer facilities are available at all registration centres to help with applications. Online awareness sessions are held on 25 October and 15 November 2025 at 7 pm; joining links are on the programme web page.

The last date for requesting an exemption for entry qualification (and submitting an Application for Evaluation of Qualifications for Exemptions) is 7 December 2025. Qualifications currently recognised for exemptions are listed in Appendix 1. If you hold a qualification not listed, download the prescribed form from the Faculty of Engineering Technology landing page under 'downloads' (https://bit.ly/4qRu69N) and send it with detailed documents to the Programme Coordinator well before the deadline. The faculty then decides whether the qualification can be considered for exemptions. Any qualification claimed in lieu of A/L must be equivalent to SLQF Level 2, a two-year full-time course. The last date for claiming approved exemptions is 20 May 2026 at the Colombo Regional Centre.

All applicants must pass a Selection Test to become eligible to register. The test is on 04 January 2026, 9 am to 11 am, at OUSL Regional Centres and Study Centres. Successful candidates are informed officially by email and called for registration; the final list is also published on the OUSL main webpage under selection test results. Any sudden changes are notified via the Induction Program LMS and the Faculty of Engineering Technology webpage (https://ou.ac.lk/programme/bachelor-of-software-engineering-honours/).

All applicants are enrolled in an Induction Program delivered through an LMS; access details are sent to the email address given in the application, so applicants must check that email regularly. The programme helps applicants understand the challenges of the BSE programme and points them to free online resources for programming, mathematics and English. There is NO ADDITIONAL FEE. Selection Test information, including practice papers, is delivered through this LMS, which also answers applicants' questions. It also starts applicants on the Future Careers Bridge, SLASSCOM's employment portal for the software industry (the website is being upgraded and is expected to be active again in November 2026).

Tentative registration schedule (all Regional Centres and Study Centres): New Registration - 14, 17, 18 and 19 February 2026. Re-Registration - 14, 17, 18, 19 and 20 March 2026. Add/Drop Courses - June 2026. Drop Courses only - July 2026. Other tentative dates: StART@OUSL commences March 2026 (regional centres and online); academic activities commence 25 April 2026; last date for obtaining studentship is 01 August 2026; the application for award of the Degree/Higher Diploma must be made online within one month of the release of Final Exam results (exact date announced on the Faculty of Engineering Technology web page).

Selected candidates are called for registration at RCs/SCs. You receive a voucher for payment of course fees and other fees. On registration day, present the payment receipt and your original certificates at the counselling desk. You are offered courses based on qualifications you already possess. Counselling is given before registration so you can decide how many courses to take in the first year (Semesters 1 and 2); some students take a lower load and plan to complete in more than four years due to background, employment or finances. After registration an official email address is generated and sent to your personal email; you must activate it and use it for all future university communication. You also receive instructions to create a Microsoft Teams account.

START@OUSL is the official OUSL Orientation Programme for new students and begins after registration. It consists of one course, FDE3023 Empowering for Independent Learning (EfIL), which teaches how to study independently in Open and Distance Learning mode. All new students MUST register for FDE3023 and complete it during the orientation programme. It is a continuing education course: it does not count in GPA and its credits do not count towards category totals. Passing EfIL is a prerequisite for registering for Level 5 and 6 courses (concurrent registration is allowed for Levels 3 and 4).

Students who have not passed Combined Mathematics (or an equivalent subject in International A/Ls) at GCE A/L MUST register for and pass MHZ2250 Elementary Mathematics for Computing in the First Semester before registering for other Mathematics courses in the degree. MHZ2250 is a continuing education course (not counted in GPA or category totals). It is a prerequisite or co-requisite for MHZ3356 Mathematics for Computing I. Students with Combined or Pure Mathematics passed at A/L are exempted from MHZ2250.

English is the only language of the BSE programme. All students must register for and complete English for Academic Purposes (EAP), a separate programme offered by the Department of English Language Teaching (DELT), starting in the first week of July 2026. EAP has three levels (Elementary, Intermediate, Advanced); placement depends on O/L and A/L English results. LTE34SE (Elementary) is exempted for students with a B grade or better in O/L English, a C or better in A/L General English, or an S in A/L English as a main subject; these students register directly for LTE34SI (Intermediate). LTE34SE has no prerequisites; LTE34SI requires LTE34SE (pass). Students with listed English qualifications in Appendix 1 (e.g. IELTS overall 5.0 academic or 5.5 general with at least 4.0 in writing, English-medium A/L, English-medium degree) are exempted from EAP and LTE34SI.

Fees: Registration fee Rs. 500; Facilities fee Rs. 2,500; Library Facilities fee Rs. 100; Per-credit fee Rs. 4,190; Payment for the EAP course only (to be completed before the academic year) Rs. 5,500. New students are recommended to offer 31 credits in the first year. Example first-year fee: 31 x 4190 + 500 + 2500 + 100 = Rs. 132,990.

Course fees can be paid in two instalments. The first instalment covers 60% of the course fee plus the registration, facilities and library fees (Rs. 3,100). For 31 credits the first instalment is 31 x 4190 x 0.6 + 3100 = Rs. 81,034 (the guidebook text says 'if you register for 30 credits' but the calculation uses 31). The voucher for the second instalment is emailed or sent via SMS by the middle of the year.

Students can change registered courses during the Add-Drop period, typically about one month after the First Semester starts; fees paid for a course dropped in this period are refunded to the student's account. The Drop date is approximately 2 months after academic activities start; a course dropped by then does not affect the grade. Course fees are NOT refunded for courses dropped after the Drop Date. If you do not drop a course and do not obtain sufficient continuous assessment marks, you are considered to have failed it and cannot sit the Final Examination. You must then pay the full course fee when registering for it next year; it is marked as a repeat course and you can obtain only a C grade when you pay and register again.

Students who withdraw from the programme before registration (before the record book is issued) are refunded the total amount minus Rs. 1,000 administration cost. Students who withdraw after registration but before the add/drop period receive 90% of the course fee (10% is deducted for administration).

OUSL grants four types of scholarships: Mahapola, University bursary, Enrolment bursary and Enhancement bursary (details at https://ou.ac.lk/scholarships/). Registered students can apply for the laptop loan from People's Bank (information on the Ministry of Higher Education website, https://www.mohe.gov.lk/). Loans to pay course fees are available from People's Bank and Commercial Bank (https://ou.ac.lk/educational-loans-for-ousl-students/).

A course code encodes department, category, level, credit rating and serial number. Example EEI3467: EE = Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering; I = Industrial category; 3 = Level 3; 4 = credit value of four; 67 = serial number. Department codes: EE Electrical and Computer, AG Agriculture and Plantation, CV Civil, DM Mechanical, MH Mathematics and Philosophy, TA Textile and Apparel Technology, LL Legal Studies, LT English Language Teaching. The code VT denotes a virtual course: students cannot enrol in it, but when they hold a qualification that cannot be exempted against an existing course, they gain credits in the appropriate category and level via the virtual course.

Course category letters: S Engineering, Y Projects, Z Mathematics, I Industrial, M Management, J General, W Industrial training, L Language. (Degree tables also use R for Project courses and E for Language.) Courses have Levels 3 to 6: Level 3 is the first undergraduate level and Level 6 the highest. One credit equals approximately 50 notional hours of study. The maximum credits a student can earn in one academic year is 38. A minimum of 125 credits is required to complete the BSEHons degree.

Prerequisite notation: CR = Concurrent Registration; P = Pass; CA = Continuous Assessment Pass. Level prerequisites: Level 3 courses require FDE3023 [CR] and LTE34SE [CR]. Level 4 courses require FDE3023 [CR] and LTE34SI [CR]. Level 5 and 6 courses require FDE3023 [P] and LTE34SI [P]. In other words, passing LTE34SE is needed to register for Level 4 (per the course-list note) and passing EfIL and LTE34SI is required for Levels 5 and 6. To register for any course you must satisfy its prerequisites by exemption or by successful completion.

Level 3 compulsory courses (recommended for Year 1). Semester 1: EEI3372 Programming in Python (3 credits, no prerequisite); EEI3366 Database Systems (3, none); EEI3346 Web Application Development (3, none); EEI3467 Software Engineering Concepts and Programming (4, none); LTE34SI English for Academic Purposes - Intermediate (4, prerequisite LTE34SE (P), runs in semesters 1 and 2). Semester 2: EEI3347 Web Technology (3, prerequisite EEI3346 (CR)); EEI3262 Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming (2, none); EEI3269 Mobile Application Design (2, none); EEL3263 Communication Skills (2, none); EEI3273 Communication and Computer Technology (2, prerequisite EEI3467 (CR)); MHZ3356 Mathematics for Computing I (3, prerequisite MHZ2250 (CR)). Year 1 compulsory credits: Semester 1 = 15, Semester 2 = 16. Level 3 elective: EEM3366 Introduction to Business Studies (3 credits, no prerequisite, offered in semester 2 or 4); it is the recommended course for students who wish to exit with the Diploma in Software Development.

Semester 4: EEI4361 User Experience Engineering (3; EEI3269 (CA), EEI3346 (CA), pass in 8 credits); EEI4362 Object Oriented Design (3; EEI3262 (CA), EEI3467 (CA), pass in 8 credits); CVM4402 Accounting for Engineers (4; pass in 18 credits at Level 3); MHZ4377 Applied Statistics (3; MHZ4359 (CR)); EER4189 Software Design in Group (1; EEI4267 (CR), pass in 20 credits at Level 3). Level 4 elective courses: EEI4369 Mobile App Development with Android (3 credits, semester 3; prerequisites EEI3269 (CA), EEI3262 (CA), EEI3366 (CA), CA in 8 credits at Level 3). Following EEI4369 requires a computer with special specifications for online lab work; on-site labs are held only on weekdays 9am-4pm at the Colombo Centre; register only if you have eligibility (CA) for EEI3269. EEI4373 Data Science (3, semester 4; EEI3366 (CA), EEI5466 (CR), MHZ4377 (CR), CA in 8 credits at Level 3). EER4489 Higher Diploma Project - Software Engineering (4 credits, semesters 5 and 6; EER4189 (CR), 45 credits pass) is offered only if there is a justification acceptable to the Department for not registering for the industrial training module. Year 2 elective credits: Semester 3 = 3, Semester 4 = 3.

Level 5 compulsory courses (recommended for Year 3). Semester 5: EEI5263 Computer Organization and Architecture (2 credits; EEI3273 (P), MHZ3356 (P), 24 credits pass in Level 3, 15 credits (CA) at Level 4); EEI5466 Advanced Database Systems (4; EEI3366 (CA), EEI3467 (CA), pass in 8 credits); EEI5467 Software Testing and Quality Assurance (4; EEI3467 (P), EEI3346 (P), EEI3366 (P), 15 credits CA at Level 4); EER5289 Research Methodology and Project Identification (2; EEL3263 (P), EEI4365 (CA), EER4189 (CA), pass 24 credits in L3, CA in 15 credits at L4); MHJ5383 Technology, Society and Environment (3; 24 credits (P) at Level 3); LLM5281 Basic Laws Relating to Engineering and Technology (2; 24 credits (P) at Level 3). Semester 6: EEI5364 Data Communication (3; EEI3273 (P), MHZ3356 (P), 24 credits pass in L3, 15 credits (CA) at L4); EEW5611 Industrial Training - Software (6; EEI3467 (P), EEI4362 (CA), EEI4365 (CA), pass in 40 credits); EEI5265 Operating Systems (2; EEI3273 (P), EEI3467 (P), 24 credits pass in L3, 15 credits (CA) at L4); MHZ5375 Discrete Mathematics (3; MHZ3356 (P) and MHZ4359 (CA)). Year 3 compulsory credits: Semester 5 = 17, Semester 6 = 14.

Level 5 elective courses: EEI5378 Neural Networks and Fuzzy Logic Applications (3 credits, semester 5; EEI3372 (P), MHZ3356 (P), MHZ4359 (CA), EEI4360 (CA), pass 24 credits at L3). EEI5376 Embedded Systems and IoT (3, semester 6; EEI3366 (P), EEI3372 (P), EEI3273 (P), pass 24 credits at L3, CA in 15 credits at L4); labs for EEI5376 are held at the CRC only. MHJ5282 History of Technology (2, semester 6; 24 credits (P) at Level 3). Year 3 elective credits: Semester 5 = 3, Semester 6 = 5.

Level 6 compulsory courses (recommended for Year 4). Semester 7: EEI6360 Software Project Management (3 credits; EEL3263 (P), EEI3467 (P), EEI5467 (CA), pass 45 credits in Levels 3 and 4, CA in 15 credits in Level 5); EEI6373 Performance Modelling (3; EEI3346 (P), EEI3347 (P), MHZ4377 (P), EEI5466 (CA), EEI5467 (CA), CA in 15 credits in Level 5); EEI6567 Software Architecture and Design (5, semesters 7 and 8; EEI3467 (P), EEI3347 (P), EEI4362 (P), pass 45 credits in Levels 3 and 4, CA in 15 credits in Level 5); EER6689 Final Project - Software Engineering (6, semesters 7 and 8; EER4189 (P), EER5289 (CA), EEI6360 (CR), EEI6567 (CR), pass in 75 credits). Semester 8: EEI6171 Emerging Technologies (1; EEL3263 (P), EEI4360 (P), pass 45 credits in L3 and L4, CA in 15 credits in L5); EEM6202 Professional Practice (2; EEL3263 (P), pass 45 credits in L3 and L4, CA in 15 credits in L5). Year 4 compulsory credits: Semester 7 = 11.5, Semester 8 = 8.5.

A minimum of 10 credits of elective courses is required from Level 6. Options: EEI6279 Natural Language Processing (2 credits, sem 7; EEI3467 (P), EEI4365 (P), MHZ5375 (CA), pass 50 credits in L3 and L4); EEI6280 Creative Design (2, sem 7; EEI3346 (P), EEI3347 (P), EEI3269 (P), EEI4360 (P), pass 50 credits in L3 and L4); EEI6366 Big Data Technologies and Distributed Systems (3, sem 7; EEI3366 (P), EEI5466 (CA), pass 50 credits in L3 and L4); EEI6363 Compiler Construction (3, sem 7 and 8; EEI4365 (P), EEI5263 (CA), MHZ5375 (CA), pass 50 credits in L3 and L4); EEI6377 Data Mining (3, sem 8; MHZ4377 (P), EEI5466 (CA), EEI4373 (P), pass 50 credits in L3 and L4); EEI6369 Cloud Computing (3, sem 8; EEI3467 (P), EEI3372 (P), EEI3273 (P), EEI4362 (CA), pass 50 credits in L3 and L4). Year 4 elective credits: Semester 7 = 8.5, Semester 8 = 7.5.

It is mandatory to complete a minimum of 6 months of full-time on-site industrial training at a software company (course EEW5611 Industrial Training - Software, 6 credits, Level 5, semester 6). SLASSCOM has asked member companies to offer placements to OUSL students and the University forwards student CVs to companies through SLASSCOM; the companies decide the selection criteria, usually a technical test and/or interview. If you are already employed or have secured a placement on your own, discuss it with your Manager/CITES; if the company's credentials are acceptable to the University you may train there. To claim an exemption for training based on existing work experience, you must register for EEW5611 Industrial Training. Students unable to complete industrial training may be offered the Higher Diploma Project (EER4489) instead, but only with a justification acceptable to the Department. Students are encouraged to begin the Future Careers Bridge Fundamental Challenges (site expected to be available in November 2026).

Each course is assessed separately using two components: Continuous Assessment (CA) and the Final Examination. CA activities include Tutor Marked Assignments (TMAs), laboratory work, mini projects, case studies, presentation sessions, Online Quizzes (OQs) and Continuous Assessment Tests (CATs), depending on the course. Except for Mathematics courses, every course has at least one CA component assessed by viva voce (face-to-face, online or on-site).

To sit the Final examination you must obtain at least 40% for the Overall Continuous Assessment Mark (OCAM), calculated by a course-specific formula, and you must apply for the Final exam through the MyOUSL portal. All Final examinations are conducted on-site on weekdays and weekends. Example for EEI3467: if Mini-Project mark MP >= 40 then X = CAT*0.3 + OQ*0.1 + MP*0.3 + LABT*0.3, otherwise X = 0; eligibility requires X >= 40 AND MP >= 40 (X = OCAM, LABT = lab test mark). In some courses such as EEI3262 the critical component is the lab test rather than the mini project: X = CAT*0.4 + OQ*0.1 + LAB*0.5, and the lab mark must be >= 40 to gain eligibility. Failing to meet eligibility means you must repeat the course.

There are strict deadlines for submitting mini-project reports, design reports and similar work. Late submissions are NOT accepted, even if the report is excellent. Because there are 6-7 courses per semester, final submission deadlines are spread out, but deadlines will not be extended just because the eligibility due date is later; if required assessments are not submitted on time you must repeat the course. Students are strongly advised to make a summary timetable of submission dates at the start of each course and keep to it.

Regulation 5.1: the Overall Assessment Mark Z% for a course (other than training courses) is computed from the Overall Continuous Assessment Mark X% and the Final Examination mark Y%. If Y >= 40 and X >= 40, then Z = 0.5X + 0.5Y. If Y < 40, then Z = Y. Regulation 5.2: for Industrial Training courses, Z = Y (final examination marks only), assessed by an Assessment Panel appointed by the Board of the Faculty and approved by the Senate in accordance with faculty-approved guidelines. Courses offered by other Faculties of OUSL are assessed as determined by the offering Faculty with Senate approval.

Grade and Grade Point Value (GPV) by Overall Assessment Mark Z%: 85-100 = A+ (4.0); 75-84 = A (4.0); 70-74 = A- (3.7); 63-69 = B+ (3.3); 55-62 = B (3.0); 50-54 = B- (2.7); 45-49 = C+ (2.3); 40-44 = C (2.0); 35-39 = C- (1.7); 30-34 = D+ (1.3); 20-29 = D (1.0); 0-19 = E (0.0). The pass grades are A+, A, A-, B+, B, B-, C+ and C. GPA is calculated from course grades and their credit ratings; continuing education courses (EfIL, EAP, MHZ2250) are not counted in GPA.

To earn the BSEHons degree a student needs 125 credits from Level 3 and above, meeting each category's minimum and not exceeding its maximum (Table 1). Industrial (I) and Engineering Sciences (S) together: minimum 67, maximum 78 credits. Management (M): 11 to 20. General (J): 3 to 6. Mathematics (Z): 12 (min and max). Project (R): minimum 9 (with at least 6 credits at Level 6), maximum 13 (with at least 6 at Level 6). Language (L, E): 6. Industrial Training (W): 6. Total 125, with at least 63 credits at Levels 5 and 6, of which at least 30 credits are at Level 6. Credits above a category maximum are not counted.

Regulations 6.8-6.11: A Pass in the BSEHons degree requires 125 course credits from Levels 3 to 6 as per Table 1 with a GPA of 2.00 or above. Second Class (Lower Division) requires a Pass with GPA 3.00 or above. Second Class (Upper Division) requires a Pass with GPA 3.30 or above. First Class requires a Pass with GPA 3.70 or above. The credits must be acquired within the minimum of 4 and maximum of 12 consecutive academic years from first registration (Regulation 6.4).

Regulation 6.8.2: course credits counted towards the degree may not exceed the maximum for any category in Table 1. If a student has excess credits in a category, the excess is eliminated by considering Level 3 courses first, then Levels 4, 5 and 6, while ensuring the maximum possible credits are counted in each category. Eliminated courses cannot be among the compulsory course combinations in Schedule 1(a) of the Regulation. Regulation 6.8.3: acquisition of credits is subject to Schedule 1(d), which lists 'Excluded Combinations of Courses'.

Regardless of exemptions granted, a student must earn by successful completion under the Scheme of Assessment at least the following credits for the Honours Degree: 15 credits at Level 6 (all categories); 31 credits at Levels 5 and 6 combined (all categories); and 63 credits in total across Levels 3 to 6 (all categories).

The Higher Diploma in Software Engineering is an intermediate qualification on the pathway to the degree. Minimum credits earned by successful completion: 15 at Level 4 or above (all categories); 8 at Level 4 in S and I categories; 15 at Levels 3 and 4 in S and I categories; 32 in total across Levels 3 to 6. Table 2 requirements: Industrial/Engineering Sciences (I, S) 30 to 45 credits (minimum 30 at Levels 3 and 4, of which at least 15 at Level 4); Management 6-12; General 0-8; Mathematics 6-12; Project/Industrial Training 4-6; Language 2-6; total 63 credits with at least 30 at Level 4 or above. Industrial Training (6 credits) or the Higher Diploma Project (4 credits) is compulsory; only those unable to complete Industrial Training are offered the Higher Diploma Project.

The Diploma in Software Development (called Diploma in Software Engineering in the Dean's message) is an exit qualification, available only if a student wishes to exit the degree programme. Minimum requirements by successful completion: 15 credits at Levels 3 and 4 (all categories); 2 credits at Level 3 in Management (M); 7 credits at Level 3 in S and I categories. Table 3: Industrial/Engineering Sciences (I, S) 14 credits at Level 3 minimum, max 25; Management 3 credits at Level 3 or 4, max 6; Mathematics 0-6; Language 0-4; total 30 credits. Compulsory courses (Table 4, Level 3): EEL3263 Communication Skills; EEI3346 Web Application Development; EEI3262 Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming; EEI3366 Database Systems; EEI3273 Communication and Computer Technology (prerequisites AGM3263 (CR), EEI3467 (CR)); EEI3467 Software Engineering Concepts and Programming. A candidate who qualifies for the Diploma receives it on the agreement that he/she cancels registration for the BSEHons degree programme.

Students unable to complete the Honours degree within the maximum of twelve consecutive academic years from first registration are awarded the Bachelor of Software Engineering Degree at SLQF Level 5 as a fallback option, after meeting Table 5: Industrial Studies (I) and Engineering Sciences (S) together 50 credits (minimum 15 at Level 5 or above); Management 5; General/Humanities 3; Mathematics 6; Projects 6; Industrial Training (W); total minimum 90 SLQF credits, with at least 30 at Level 5 or above.

A candidate eligible for the BSEHons degree must supplicate on the prescribed form to the Deputy Registrar / Senior Assistant Registrar / Assistant Registrar of Examinations before the date set by the university. The application for award of the Degree or Higher Diploma is made online within one month of the release of Final Exam results; the exact date is announced on the Faculty of Engineering Technology web page.

Qualifications that exempt a student from EAP and LTE34SI include: a Bachelor's degree, Postgraduate Diploma or Master's degree in English medium; UTEL score of at least band 6.00 in all four skills; IELTS overall 5.0 (academic) or 5.5 (general) with at least 4.00 in writing; TOEFL paper-based overall 450 with 3.5 in writing, computer-based overall 200 with 3.5 in writing, or internet-based overall 90 with writing 20 or above; Advanced Level completed in English medium (local, or London Edexcel/Cambridge A/L in English medium); National Diploma in Teaching (English) from NCOE/NIE; HND in English (SLIATE); Diploma in English from a recognised university; Diploma in Library and Information Science (English medium) by the Sri Lanka Library Association; English as a subject at G.C.E. A/L (not General English); Diploma in English Language and Literature or Advanced Certificate in English by the Department of Language Studies; National Diploma in Technology (NDT), Institute of Technology, University of Moratuwa.

Exemptions by qualification (courses exempted): Combined or Pure Mathematics passed at A/L -> MHZ2250. OUSL [Higher] Diploma in Technology - Civil, Textile, Agriculture -> VTI3F00, MHZ3356. OUSL [Higher] Diploma in Technology - Electrical, Electronics, Mechanical, Mechatronics -> VTI3F00, MHZ3356, EEI3273. BCS (British Computer Society) Certificate -> VTI3F00, EEI3467. CMA Stage I or II -> VTI3G00. CIMA Stage I or II -> VTI3G00. Qualifications not listed can be evaluated using the exemption form on the faculty landing page.

The Student Welfare (Affairs) Division keeps personal and academic records of all OUSL students. Notify in writing, immediately, any change of address, medium of study, study centre, civil status or courses to: Senior Assistant Registrar, Student Welfare Division, The Open University of Sri Lanka, P. O. Box 21, Nawala, Nugegoda - 10250. Include your name, registration number, programme of study and contact details (email and/or phone). You must also give your contact numbers and email to the Programme Coordinator at the BSEHons office and notify them immediately of any changes.

Computer laboratories at many Regional and Study Centres are free for OUSL students, with a monthly time quota. Each has about 25 computers with internet, printers, scanners, video conferencing, wireless access and photocopying. A student registered at ANY centre can use the facilities at ANY OTHER centre, so register at the centre most convenient for your academic and administrative needs; there is nothing special about registering at Colombo. Regional centres have a centre code ending in 0. Centres include Kandy CP20, Hatton CP21, Batticaloa EP60, Ampara EP61, Trincomalee EP62, Anuradhapura NC50, Polonnaruwa NC51, Jaffna NP40, Vavuniya NP41, Kilinochchi NP42, Mullaitivu NP43, Mannar NP44, Kurunegala NW70, Puttalam NW71, Naththandiya NW73, Ratnapura SG90, Kegalle SG91, Matara SP30, Ambalangoda SP31, Galle SP32, Ambalantota SP33, Badulla UP80, Bandarawela UP81, Monaragala UP82, Colombo WP10, Gampaha WP11, Kalutara WP12, and Matale (CP). Locations and contacts: https://ou.ac.lk/res/.

Students can use the main library at Nawala, Colombo, and regional libraries at Anuradhapura, Batticaloa, Jaffna, Kandy and Matara. Lending is limited to two books at a time and requires a deposit. The library is open year-round except the seven University holidays and a few days around Sinhala and Tamil New Year and Christmas. It has an Audio-Visual Resource Centre, internet, Wi-Fi and photocopying. Study centres have small reference collections.

Temporary residential facilities (TRF) are offered at the Colombo, Kandy and Matara Regional Centres for a limited number of students participating in approved academic activities. To request one, get the TRF form certified by the relevant academic coordinator or a senior academic staff member of the department, by producing your student record book.

University holidays: Thai Pongal Day, Independence Day, Sinhala and Tamil New Year Day, May Day, Vesak Poya Day, Holy Prophet's Birthday and Christmas Day. Other than on University holidays, activities may be held on any other day of the year, including weekends; the University tries to schedule activities on weekends and public holidays, but lab sessions and on-site CATs/Final examinations may be on weekdays. The activity schedule is given at the start of the academic year, so plan ahead.

OUSL, established under the Universities Act No. 16 of 1978, is the only recognised university in Sri Lanka offering education through distance learning and has the same legal and academic status as other national universities. It has six faculties (Engineering Technology, Natural Sciences, Humanities and Social Sciences, Education, Health Sciences, Management Studies), nine Regional Centres (Anuradhapura, Badulla, Batticaloa, Colombo, Jaffna, Kandy, Kurunegala, Matara, Ratnapura) and 19 Study Centres. The Faculty of Engineering Technology has six departments; the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering offers BSEHons, a Higher Diploma in Technology, BSc Honours in Engineering and research degrees, and has offered a Master's in Data Science since January 2025. CITES was established in 2021 with seed funding from AHEAD.

Programme educational outcomes: produce competent software engineers with up-to-date knowledge and ingenuity to address software engineering problems holistically with consideration for environment and society, and with inspiration to lead their specialty areas through continuous professional development and research. Career paths include Software Engineer or AI/Machine Learning Engineer progressing to Tech Lead, then Project Manager or Software Architect; or Tester/QA Engineer progressing to QA Lead, QA Manager or Quality Analyst. Students are encouraged to join the Software Engineering Society (SESoc) for leadership development and industry networking.
